gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-satoshi: Satoshi reads tall and approachable, every stroke cut to a single width with an e that stays open instead of pinching shut. Noto Serif Sinhala above it adds a literary, gently modulated voice.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-switzer: Refined is the first word for Noto Serif Sinhala, whose strokes swell and thin only mildly above its Swiss-minded partner. Switzer follows in wire-like, pencil-line sans-serif letters, and that gap in texture is what the pair does best.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-work-sans: A tall middle zone in every word gives Noto Serif Sinhala its literary look, with thread-thin hairlines against slightly thicker stems. And Work Sans lays down a level, modern beat beneath it, with no accents of weight at all.
gen-gf-noto-serif-telugu-archivo: Authoritative describes Noto Serif Telugu, a serif whose lowercase body nearly meets the ascenders and whose curves thicken only modestly. Archivo then carries the text with a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, giving long lines an editorial, approachable pace.
gen-gf-noto-serif-telugu-fs-asap: Noto Serif Telugu has a lowercase body that nearly meets the ascenders, with medium-range stroke modulation giving every curve a dignified shape. Asap answers in low-contrast sans-serif lines with open arcs, easy going over many paragraphs.
gen-gf-noto-serif-telugu-fs-epilogue: Epilogue brings curvy, unclamped letters with a wire-like monoline skeleton and stubby ascender tips. Epilogue against Noto Serif Telugu, whose strokes thin like soft-metal type, makes the strongest quality here a clear change of texture.
gen-gf-noto-serif-telugu-fs-fira-sans: Noto Serif Telugu keeps a faint pull between heavy verticals and lighter horizontals. Fira Sans sits beneath it in true monoline, with a generous x-height and s curves opening wide at both ends, so dignified serif shapes and clean sans lines share the page without crowding.
gen-gf-noto-serif-telugu-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase body and broad open counters on its c and s, which gives it a trustworthy, sturdy look. Noto Serif Telugu, with its brushed-watercolor line shifts, keeps the heading dignified.
gen-gf-noto-serif-telugu-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a thick, heavy-looking strip of crisp text through the middle, its letters held open rather than curled shut. Noto Serif Telugu contrasts with lightly engraved, brass-like modulation, so slightly larger heading sizes feel natural.
gen-gf-noto-serif-telugu-general-sans: General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure with an x-height that fills the line, and its curves have no stress at all. But Noto Serif Telugu brings subdued contrast and authority, while the sans-serif handles smooth, unobstructed reading.
